note: Diagnostic only. PLAN.md 1.4: judge_score never drives training. A judge-only reward is trivially gamed. The binary substep grader owns the RL reward; this score is for human review only.

instruction_following.rationale: The deployed app only presents the /login route and does not demonstrate any of the core features specified in the instruction. The spec requires four routes (/login, /, /habits, /habits/:id) with habit management (create, list, rename, delete), completions (mark/unmark), streak calculation (current_streak, longest_streak), navigation with top bar and user menu, dashboard with counters, and habit detail pages with completion calendars. Only the login page is visible in all three viewport screenshots; without valid credentials to test authentication and access to protected routes, none of the core features can be verified as present or functional.
instruction_following.asks: Are the features named in instruction.md Core-features and User-flow sections actually present and reachable in the deployed app? A missing feature is a score cut, a hidden-but-implemented feature is a smaller cut. Score against the actual spec passed in, not a generic notion.

functionality.rationale: The app is completely untestable for functionality because no credentials file was provided and the login form is non-functional. Only the login screen at "/" is visible across all viewports. None of the core flows (signup/login, habit CRUD, marking completions, streak calculation) could be tested or verified. Without the ability to authenticate, the entire protected feature set remains inaccessible, making it impossible to determine if the core functionality works at all.

no evidence of any protected routes (/habits, /habits/:id) or dashboard functionality
functionality.asks: Do the core flows actually WORK when driven -- signup/login, primary CRUD, submit forms, key journeys -- without runtime errors, dead ends, blank screens, or 500s? Console errors and failed network requests during real interaction count heavily.

ux_flow.rationale: The app fails to meet most UX flow requirements from the spec. Evidence shows only the /login route is reachable and displays a sign-in form, but no credentials were available to test authentication flows. Critical missing elements include: no post-login navigation (Dashboard and Habits links), no redirect behavior for unauthenticated users visiting protected routes (spec requires ?next= param), no visible top bar with user email and Sign out link, no evidence of the four required journeys (daily check-in, add habit, fix mistake, remove habit), and no demonstration of required states (loading skeletons, empty states, error states, business-rule rejection messages, or toasts). Without login credentials and with only route / visited, the complete navigation reachability and redirect flows cannot be verified.
evidence: login_status: 'no credentials file' - cannot test authenticated flows
a11y_probes landmarks show 0 nav, 0 header elements - no top bar navigation present
ux_flow.asks: Navigation reachability, empty states, loading states, error states, feedback on actions (toasts/inline messages), sensible redirects (unauth -> login?next=, login success -> next/home). Judge against the spec's User flow section.

ui_visual.rationale: The visual design closely follows the spec with correct palette values (background #FAF9F7 rgb(250,249,247), primary text #111827 rgb(17,24,39), muted text #6B7280 rgb(107,114,128), primary CTA #4F46E5 rgb(79,70,229)), proper Inter font family, 8px border radius on inputs/buttons, and a 2px indigo focus ring (rgb(79,70,229)). However, there are gaps: body font-size is 16px instead of the specified 14px, h1 is 24px instead of 28px, h2 is 18px with line-height 28px instead of 22px/1.25, and transitions use cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) instead of the specified cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1). Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion correctly.
evidence: focus_walk input box_shadow: rgb(79, 70, 229) 0px 0px 0px 2px confirms 2px indigo ring
motion_with_reduced_motion transitions all|1e-05s confirms reduced-motion respected
ui_visual.asks: Does the visual design match the UI/UX notes section -- palette hex values, type scale, radii, density, hierarchy? Does it look intentionally designed, or default-Bootstrap / default-Tailwind / default-shadcn slop? Use computed styles as objective evidence, not just screenshots.

motion.rationale: The app has minimal motion implementation that deviates significantly from the spec. Without prefers-reduced-motion, only one transition was detected with 0.15s duration and cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) easing, which does not match the spec's required 150ms/250ms with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). While the app does respond to prefers-reduced-motion by changing transitions to 1e-05s (effectively disabling them), the base motion system is not implemented per spec and evidence is limited to only the login page.
evidence: motion./.transitions shows only 1 element with 'color, background-color, border-color, text-decoration-color, fill, stroke|0.15s|cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)' - wrong duration (0.15s vs spec 150ms is close but easing cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) does not match spec cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1))
motion_with_reduced_motion./.transitions shows 27 elements with 'all|1e-05s|ease' - confirms prefers-reduced-motion is respected by effectively disabling transitions
Only route / (login page) was tested; no evidence of motion on interactive states like dashboard tiles, habit toggles, modals, or toasts mentioned in spec
motion.asks: Are transitions present with durations and easing near the spec (typically 150ms / 250ms / cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1))? Does the app respect prefers-reduced-motion when emulated? Zero motion is a cut; bouncy over-motion is also a cut if the spec forbids it.

accessibility.rationale: The app demonstrates strong accessibility fundamentals with visible focus indicators (2px indigo box-shadow on inputs, auto outline on buttons), labeled form inputs (no unlabeled inputs detected), and respects prefers-reduced-motion (transitions reduce to 1e-05s when enabled). Body text meets WCAG AA contrast at 4.5:1+ (rgb(17,24,39) on rgb(250,249,247)). However, there are minor gaps: no semantic landmarks (main, nav, header) detected on the login page, and only the login route could be tested due to lack of credentials, limiting full keyboard navigation verification across the authenticated app.

accessibility.asks: Visible focus indicator on Tab through, labels on icon buttons, WCAG AA text contrast (4.5:1 body), keyboard reachability. Judge against the spec's stated a11y bar.

responsiveness.rationale: The login page renders cleanly across all tested viewports (1920x1200, 768x1024, 390x844) with no horizontal overflow, overlapping elements, or hidden CTAs. The centered sign-in card adapts appropriately to each screen size, maintaining proper spacing and touch-target sizing. All interactive elements remain fully accessible and properly sized at mobile (390px) and tablet (768px) breakpoints.
responsiveness.asks: Does the layout hold at the mobile and tablet viewports without horizontal overflow, overlapping elements, hidden CTAs, or squashed tables? Judge from multi-viewport screenshots.
